newsitem.title: USA: Ontario Hydro nuke power unit returns to service.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro nuke power unit returns to service.

text.p: A sixth nuclear power unit at Ontario Hydro's eight-unit Pickering station resumed electricity production this week as expected, a company spokesman said Thursday.
Ontario Hydro has been returning the 540 megawatt (MW) Pickering units to service from a plant-wide shutdown April 20 due to a problem with a backup valve on an emergency cooling system.
A sixth unit at the station was producing about 489 MW as of early Thursday and was being ramped up to full power, said spokesman Al Manchee.
Another of the six operating units was producing at near 40 percent power for some short-term maintenance, he said.
The remaining two idled units at the plant were scheduled to return to operation in March of 1997.
Also, one of four 930 MW units at the Darlington nuclear power plant was expected to be off line into late November due to some valve work, Manchee said.
The remaining three Darlington units were operating normally, the spokesman said.
Both Darlington and Pickering are located east of Toronto, Ontario.

Ontario Hydro has an overall in-service generation capacity of just over 29,000 MW. During October the company typically generates about 16,000 MW of power, of which five to six percent is exported to the U.S..
Demand for Ontario Hydro's electricity typically peaks in December and January, with record demand of near 24,000 MW set January 19, 1994.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
